text:
tara: Noticed a spike in internal TLS failures after we applied the keystore keypolicy tighten. ~0.4% for ap-northeast -> ap-southeast. Logs show KMS AccessDenied on Unwrap.

liam: Can you paste the error lines? Could be SourceVpc condition mismatch after yesterday's NAT remap.

tara: snippet:
2026-02-18T14:07:12Z ERROR tls: server handshake failed peer=svc-cache region=ap-southeast-1: unwrap error: KMS.AccessDenied principal=arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/keystore-unwrapper/keystore-pod context: sourceVpc=vpc-0f9e8d7c

zhou: We did lock key policy to vpc-0a1b2c3d. Egress change moved those pods via NAT in vpc-0f9e8d7c. kms-bot: KeyPolicyMismatch alert for key ef12-34ab, proposed remediation: add new VPC to policy or switch to IAM-principal binding.

liam: Short fix: patch key policy to include both vpcs and canary restart 2 pods. Long-term: move off aws:SourceVpc conditions and use kms:EncryptionContext + IAM principal.

tara: Patch applied at 14:12, canary restarted 14:15. Handshake failures fell to baseline within 3 minutes. Opening follow-ups: KEYS-412 (policy CI), NET-240 (egress mapping audit).

zhou: Also add a predeploy check to simulate unwrap from each cluster to catch this earlier.
